message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most celebrated and influential composers who have made their mark in the United States:

| Composer | Era / Style | Notable Works |
|----------|-------------|---------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | Jazz‑influenced classical | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | Neoclassical, “American” sound | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | Broadway, symphonic | *West Side Story*, *Candide* |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks* |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film scores | *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park* |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | Minimalism | *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910–1981) | Romantic/Modern | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* |
| **Charles Ives** (1874–1954) | Experimental, early modern | *The Unanswered Question*, *Concord Sonata* |
| **William Grant Still** (1895–1978) | African‑American composer, “Third Stream” | *Afro-American Symphony*, *Bluebird* |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | Post‑minimalist | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* |

These figures span a wide range of styles—from jazz-inflected classics to avant‑garde minimalism—and each has helped shape what we think of as “American music.”
